meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_62_packages.json, all reference===62 edges from torahData.js, and the full source text torah_62.txt. Every line was scanned for bechina-language markers (בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ, נִקְרָא, דָּא, זֶה בְּחִינַת, הִיא). Concepts appearing in explicit bechina formulations that are absent from the reference=62 bechina edge dataset were flagged. Concepts that are part of a new independent domain (3+ nodes with explicit bechina language) are flagged for torah_62_new_packages.json.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 23: 'וּדְבֵקוּת אֲחוֹרֵי הַקְּדֻשָּׁה, הִיא עַל יְדֵי הַתַּעֲנִית' — this states that fasting IS the means of cleaving to the back of holiness. This is an EITZA formulation (through fasting one achieves clinging), not a bechina equivalence (fasting IS NOT = clinging; fasting PRODUCES clinging). There is an existing eitza edge (id=707) in the dataset for this relationship. Correctly classified as eitza, not a bechina gap.

Lines 23 and 27 describe the technical procedure of writing the name of God backwards (יוד, יוד-הא, יוד-הא-ואו, etc.) as an analogy for how fasting works. This is a PROOF-TEXT ILLUSTRATION, not a bechina statement equating two concepts. The numerical equivalence (הויה + אלקים backwards = 272 = רעב) IS a genuine bechina and is flagged above. The writing procedure itself is the analogical explanation, not the conceptual equation.

Line 48: 'וַיַּסֵּב לְשׁוֹן סְעֻדָּה, הַיְנוּ לְשׁוֹן הֲסִבָּה' — the Midrash says ויסב IS the language of eating/feasting. This is a midrashic etymology cited as supporting evidence for the Torah's opening thesis (that the eating of Israel creates yichud). It is not a standalone bechina between two conceptual nodes; it is a proof-text. The concept 'holy eating = yichud' (which is the deeper content) is flagged in the new packages section.
